landManager: Glacier Peak Wilderness, Entiat Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (2108 Entiat Way, Entiat, WA; 509-784-4700).
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass (or Interagency America the Beautiful Pass) for trailhead parking.
drive: Turn onto Entiat River Road just south of the town of Entiat and follow it a little over 38 miles up the valley, past Cottonwood Campground where it turns to gravel, to the trailhead a short distance beyond.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From the long pullout on the north side of SR-20 about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, via the South Buttress climbers' trail

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required to park at the Ingalls Creek Trailhead ($5/day or $30/annual).
drive: From Cle Elum, take SR-970 east 7 miles to US-97, turn north on US-97 over Blewett Pass, and at milepost 178 turn left onto Ingalls Creek Road. Cross Peshastin Creek, bear left, and follow the road to its end at the trailhead. From Leavenworth, go east on US-2 for 4 miles, turn right onto US-97 south and go 7 miles to the same turn.
From Seattle on US 2, turn left at Coles Corner and follow that road about 10 miles, then turn right onto White River Road and drive roughly 1.5 miles to a pullout on the left (the winter parking).

landManager: U.S. Forest Service
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From Darrington, drive south on the Mountain Loop Highway (FR-20) to Sloan Creek Road (FR-49) on the left, then follow FR-49 about 6.6 miles to the trailhead.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From Mount Baker Highway (SR-542) about 46.5 miles east of Bellingham, a quarter mile past the state maintenance shed, turn left onto Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32) and drive 2.1 miles to the Goat Mountain trailhead.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required — $5/day or $30/annual.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Naches Ranger District)
storedPass: No Discover Pass (national forest land)
Northwest Forest Pass ($5 day / $35 annual) or $5 day-use parking fee
drive: From US-12 past Rimrock Lake Dam onto Tieton Reservoir Road (FR-1200); park at the pullouts near the split-rail-fence spring

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Noisy-Diobsud Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: Turn north off SR 20 at milepost 82 onto the Baker Lake Highway (Forest Road 11) and drive 25.5 miles to its end at the Baker River trailhead.

landManager: National Park Service - Ross Lake National Recreation Area, North Cascades National Park Complex (peak and all US-side approaches). The drive in crosses B.C. Parks' Skagit Valley Provincial Park. NPS complex information line 360-854-7200.
storedPass: No Northwest Forest Pass or Discover Pass. You do need a passport or NEXUS card, because the entire drive is through Canada and you must enter and re-enter the US at a staffed port of entry - Hozomeen is not one.
No US trailhead pass. Passport or NEXUS required; the drive is through Canada and re-entry must be at a staffed port of entry, which Hozomeen is not.

landManager: Split management: the East Bank Trailhead and the East Bank Trail are in Ross Lake National Recreation Area, part of the North Cascades National Park Complex (National Park Service). Jack Mountain itself and the Nohokomeen Glacier are in the Pasayten Wilderness on the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest.
storedPass: None - no pass or permit is reported to be required for the East Bank Trailhead approach.
None at the East Bank Trailhead.
drive: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east to milepost 138, where the East Bank trailhead parking is beside the highway. SR-20 is closed for winter beyond Colonial Creek.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: From I-90 Exit 52 (West Snoqualmie Pass), the Pacific Crest Trailhead (PCT northbound) lot sits just off the exit ramp on a short dirt spur (Northwest Forest Pass required; the ~50-car lot fills early on weekends).

landManager: National Park Service — Mount Rainier National Park
storedPass: Standard Mount Rainier NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7 days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
America the Beautiful / NPS annual pass accepted
drive: From the Narada Falls parking lot on the road to Paradise, plowed year-round, climb the steep hillside about 200 ft to Stevens Canyon Road; when that road is open, roughly late May to mid-October, most parties park at the Reflection Lake pullout instead and skip the climb

names: Monument Creek Trailhead (Lost River Road / Harts Pass Road)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Pasayten Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at trailheads (e.g. Andrews Creek, Chewuch River) — $5/day or $30/annual.
Not required — free self-issue wilderness permit only; no Northwest Forest Pass needed at this trailhead.
drive: From the Monument Creek Trailhead off Lost River Road past Mazama

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District

names: Robinson Creek Trailhead (Lost River Road / FR 5400)
Robinson Creek Trailhead (Lost River Road / Forest Road 5400)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Pasayten Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at the Robinson Creek trailhead (none needed at Monument Creek or Slate Pass) — $5/day or $30/annual.
Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From Winthrop drive about 15 miles west on SR 20, turn right onto Lost River Road, keep left after half a mile, and follow it about 7.5 miles on pavement, then 1.25 miles on gravel FR 5400 to the Robinson Creek Trailhead on the right.

landManager: Gifford Pinchot National Forest (Mt. Adams Ranger District) — Mount Adams Wilderness
storedPass: Cold Springs/South Climb Trailhead day-use fee: $5/vehicle/day or $30/year (a Northwest Forest Pass satisfies this; the Climbing Pass’s parking stub also covers it May 1–Sept 30).
drive: North from Trout Lake via Mt. Adams Road, Forest Road 80 and Forest Road 8040

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
None required to park at the Dosewallips road end, and no park entrance fee is charged on this approach.
drive: From the Dosewallips Road (FR-2610) washout parking near Brinnon: road-walk/bike toward the Olympics east-side trails

landManager: U.S. Forest Service
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From the Boulder Ridge Trailhead at the end of FR-1131 (~2,700 ft) off Baker Lake Road, via Boulder Ridge Trail #605

landManager: U.S. Forest Service
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From Bellingham, drive SR-542 east about 55 miles to the end of the highway. At Heather Meadows go one-way around Picture Lake past the ski lifts; the large parking area is at the end of the road on the right. The highway is plowed only to Heather Meadows outside roughly July to late September.

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From Port Angeles, take Race Street south onto Hurricane Ridge Road and climb to the Hurricane Ridge parking area; turn sharply left onto the gravel Obstruction Point Road and follow it about 8 miles to its end at the trailhead. The gravel road is generally open only from mid-July to October.

landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: None beyond the NPS backcountry permit for the overnight stay — no Northwest Forest Pass or Discover Pass applies to this approach.
North Cascades NP backcountry permit (not an America the Beautiful pass); if approaching via Chilliwack Lake Provincial Park, BC, a separate BC Parks day-use/parking arrangement may apply.
drive: From the Depot Creek trailhead (reached via the unsigned dirt spur off Chilliwack Lake Road in BC)

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at the Nason Ridge Trailhead — $5/day or $30/year; no fee at the Rock Mountain, Merritt Lake or Snowy Creek trailheads.
No fee currently required at Merritt Lake Trailhead (self-register; no toilet or water on site) — confirm before visiting since fee requirements can change.
drive: From Stevens Pass, drive US-2 east 11.3 miles and turn north onto FR-657, signed for Merritt Lake. Follow it 1.6 miles to the road's end and trailhead parking.

names: Hoh Rain Forest Trailhead (Hoh River Trail)
landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.

landManager: National Park Service
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From the Shannon Ridge Trailhead at the end of FR-1152-014 (~2,500 ft) off Baker Lake Road

landManager: Washington State Department of Natural Resources — Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area (day-use only)
storedPass: Washington State Discover Pass required to park at the Mount Si trailhead.
drive: From I-90 take Exit 32, turn left onto 436th Ave SE and follow it to SE North Bend Way; turn left, then after 0.3 mile turn right onto SE Mount Si Road and continue 2.4 miles to the trailhead entrance on the left.

landManager: Olympic National Forest (Hood Canal Ranger District)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
No parking pass or fee is needed at the Putvin Trailhead.
drive: The standard-route trailhead is the Putvin Trailhead (Trail #813) on Hamma Hamma Road (FR-25), about 11.8-12.1 miles west of Hwy 101 and about 4.5 miles past the Lena Lake trailhead, at roughly 1,600 ft elevation.

names: Depot Creek Road trailhead (via Chilliwack, BC)
landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: No US trailhead pass applies — this approach parks in British Columbia and crosses into the United States on foot. A valid passport or passport card is needed for the border crossing.
drive: From Chilliwack, BC via Chilliwack River Road ~31.7 miles, then the rough Depot Creek Road spur (high-clearance; passport required to cross the border on foot); unmaintained Depot Creek trail up-valley

names: Mount Teneriffe Trailhead (SE Mount Si Road)
landManager: Washington State Department of Natural Resources — Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area (day-use only)
storedPass: Washington State Discover Pass required to park at the Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area trailhead.
drive: From I-90 exit 32, turn left on 436th Avenue SE and go about 0.5 mile to SE North Bend Way, turn left, and after about 0.25 mile turn right onto SE Mount Si Road. Follow it 2.9 miles, past the Little Si and Mount Si trailheads, to the lot on the left.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass (or America the Beautiful interagency pass) required to park at the Tiffany Springs Campground trailhead
N/A
drive: From Winthrop, head north on East Chewuch River Road for 6.5 miles and turn right onto FR-37. Follow FR-37 for 13 miles, then turn left onto FR-39 and continue 7.5 miles to Tiffany Springs Campground.
